record.paper_title: Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems
record.original_question: For critical planar percolation, improve coarse asymptotic estimates such as R^{-5/48+o(1)} for the probability that the cluster of the origin has diameter at least R and R^{-5/4+o(1)} for the probability that a given site is pivotal for a crossing event, as well as analogous estimates for related events. In particular, obtain formulas that are sharp up to multiplicative constants, and ideally more precise asymptotics.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1. Improve the estimates R−5/48+o(1) and R−5/4+o(1) mentioned above (as well as other similar estimates) to more precise formulas. It would be especially nice to obtain estimates that are sharp up to multiplicative constants.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider critical Bernoulli site percolation on the triangular lattice in the plane (equivalently, any model in the same conformally invariant universality class). For R ≥ 1, let θ(R) denote the probability that the percolation cluster of the origin has Euclidean diameter at least R, and let π(R) denote the probability that a fixed site is pivotal for the crossing event of a box of side length R (i.e., that there exist four alternating-color arms from the site to distance R). It is known that

  θ(R) = R^{-5/48 + o(1)}  and  π(R) = R^{-5/4 + o(1)}  as R → ∞,

and analogous polynomial-with-o(1) estimates hold for other arm events (half-plane j-arm events and polychromatic j-arm events in the whole plane).

Problem: Sharpen these asymptotics. In particular, prove that θ(R) and π(R), as well as the half-plane and polychromatic j-arm probabilities, are each comparable to an explicit power of R up to multiplicative constants bounded above and below (i.e., remove the o(1) in the exponent and replace it by a quantitative power-law error or, ideally, by a true multiplicative-constant equivalence). More generally, obtain precise asymptotic formulas, including (where possible) the leading multiplicative constants.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant recent progress has been made. Du, Gao, Li, and collaborators (Comm. Math. Phys. 405:182, 2024; arXiv:2205.15901) establish sharp estimates (matching upper and lower bounds up to multiplicative constants, with power-law error bounds in most cases) for half-plane j-arm events for j ≥ 1 and polychromatic whole-plane j-arm events for j > 1 in critical planar percolation, explicitly answering a large part of the problem. The one-arm whole-plane case (the R^{-5/48} estimate for cluster diameter) is not fully covered by these results, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully resolved, and obtaining the exact multiplicative constants remains open.

status_evidence.title: Sharp Asymptotics for Arm Probabilities in Critical Planar Percolation
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp estimates on the asymptotics of the probability of half-plane j-arm events for j ≥ 1 and planar j-arm events for j>1 ... answer a large part of a question of Schramm (ICM Proc., 2006).
status_evidence.claim: Sharp asymptotics (up to multiplicative constants) established for many arm events in critical planar percolation, directly addressing the problem.

status_evidence.title: Sharp asymptotics for arm probabilities in critical planar percolation
status_evidence.snippet: We derive sharp estimates on the asymptotics of the probability of half-plane j-arm events for j ≥ 1 and planar j-arm events for j>1, with power-law error bounds in most cases.
status_evidence.claim: Power-law error bounds beyond the o(1) estimates are obtained for these arm events.

status_evidence.title: Strict inequalities for arm exponents in planar percolation
status_evidence.snippet: Further work building on sharpened arm-exponent estimates in critical 2D percolation.
status_evidence.claim: Active follow-up work indicates the problem is partially but not completely resolved.
